h1.en: Can PDRN outperform retinol on crow's feet?

deck.en: A randomised, double-blind, split-face trial of a 0.1% PDRN eye cream against 0.1% retinol in 31 women — read at source, appraised in full.

byline.en: Appraised by the Skingenetix research team. Medically reviewed by Dr Esther Bodde, Cosmetic & Medical Physician. Last reviewed 30 September 2026.

definition.en: [PDRN](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/pdrn-research) (polydeoxyribonucleotide, listed on ingredient labels as sodium DNA) is a purified mix of DNA fragments from salmon. Long used as an injectable in clinics, it is now used in creams and serums for firmer, smoother-looking skin.

answer.en: The Ye 2026 trial is a randomised, double-blind, split-face study in which 31 women with sensitive skin used a 0.1% PDRN eye cream on one side of the face and 0.1% retinol in the same base on the other, twice a day. After 28 days, crow's-feet wrinkle area and number had fallen by up to 23% on the PDRN side, against about 6–7% with retinol.

verdict.en: **Our verdict:** the only controlled trial of PDRN on intact skin, and a strong result. PDRN improved crow's feet more than twice as much as retinol within 28 days, visibly by day 14, measured by four instruments with every woman as her own comparison. It is one trial of 31 women, compared with retinol rather than a placebo, so we cite it for the ingredient as studied.

seo_description.en: In a split-face trial of 31 women, a 0.1% PDRN eye cream softened crow's feet by up to 23% in 28 days, over twice as much as 0.1% retinol.

v.en: Randomised, double-blind, split-face trial: each woman used both creams, one on each side of the face, assigned at random.
31 Chinese women aged 35 to 55 (average 47.5), all with self-reported sensitive skin and visible crow's feet, under-eye lines and eye bags.
A water-in-silicone eye cream with 0.1% PDRN-850K, a medium-length salmon PDRN, as its only active, twice a day around the eyes, with daytime sunscreen.
0.1% retinol in an identical cream base, on the other side of the same face. There was no placebo side.
28 days, with measurements at day 0, day 14 and day 28.
VISIA 7 imaging for wrinkles, Antera 3D for eye bags and tear troughs, a Cutometer for firmness and elasticity, and Ultrascan UC22 ultrasound for dermal thickness and density.
0.1% PDRN-850K (about 1,200 base pairs, up to 850 kDa, at least 96% pure), stated in the methods; 0.1% retinol on the comparison side.

No specific funding. Four authors are affiliated with commercial skincare biotechnology companies (Inertia Shanghai Biotechnology and DermaHealth Shanghai Biotechnology); the paper declares no conflicts. The PDRN came from Ruijiming (Shandong) Biotechnology.
A — randomised, double-blind and instrument-measured, with each woman as her own comparison; compared with retinol rather than a placebo.

title.en: Improvement with PDRN, compared with retinol

subtitle.en: Retinol's improvement = 1×. The paper reports these ratios as approximate; the exact statistics are in its Figure 6.

caption.en: The authors report the PDRN side improving about twice as much as the retinol side on wrinkles around the eyes, dermal thickness and density, and eye bags and tear troughs, and about 1.8 times as much on firmness and elasticity. On crow's feet, wrinkle area and number fell by about 20% to 23% with PDRN, against about 6% to 7% with retinol (Ye et al., 2026).

alt.en: A glass petri dish of pale pink solution on a rose-coloured surface

body.en: Thirty-one women with sensitive skin used two eye creams for 28 days, one on each side of the face, assigned at random. Neither they nor the assessors knew which side had which. One cream contained 0.1% PDRN, the other 0.1% retinol, in exactly the same base, so any difference between the two sides came from the active ingredient.

The skin was measured with four instruments at the start, at day 14 and at day 28, after 20 minutes' rest in a temperature- and humidity-controlled room. Alongside the clinical trial, the team tested the PDRN in skin cells and in samples of human skin damaged by UV light in the laboratory.

items.en: What it was compared with. PDRN was tested against 0.1% retinol, an established anti-ageing ingredient, in an identical base. Both sides improved, and PDRN improved more; with no placebo side, the trial measures PDRN against retinol rather than against no treatment. 0.1% retinol works gradually, and four weeks is a short run for it.
Why split-face matters. Every woman was her own comparison, which removes differences in age, diet and sun exposure between groups.

How it was measured. Four instruments measured wrinkles, eye bags, firmness and dermal density rather than judging by eye. The ratios are the authors' own approximations; the exact statistics appear in the paper's Figure 6.

What the ultrasound shows. Dermal thickness and density rose about twice as much with PDRN. The authors note that part of the day-28 change may reflect short-term hydration and plumping as well as structural change.
Scale and setting. 31 women aged 35 to 55, all with sensitive skin, around the eyes, over 28 days, in an eye cream with PDRN as its only active.
Who ran it. Four authors are affiliated with commercial skincare biotechnology companies; the paper declares no conflicts of interest and no specific funding.

heading.en: Where this trial sits in the evidence

body.en: PDRN has a long record as an injectable, but on intact skin its evidence rests on this trial: the first controlled study of a PDRN cream used without needles or microneedling. A 2026 systematic review of PDRN trials found mostly injected or procedure-assisted studies, and it was completed before this one was published ([Alhussain et al., 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42572627/)).

In the same paper, in a laboratory study on human skin samples damaged by UV light, the PDRN cream raised nine types of collagen, elastin and fibrillin: a laboratory result that fits the firmer, denser-looking skin measured on the women's faces.

Every study we rely on, graded, is on the [PDRN evidence hub](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/pdrn-research), alongside our other [ingredient research](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/the-science). For a peptide trial on crow's feet, see our appraisal of the [Argireline® trial](https://www.skingenetix.com/blogs/clinical-studies/argireline-crows-feet-trial-wang-2013).

answers.en: It shows that a 0.1% PDRN eye cream reduced crow's-feet wrinkle area and number by up to 23% in 28 days, more than twice the improvement of 0.1% retinol on the other side of the same face, measured by imaging. It is one trial of 31 women, compared with retinol rather than a placebo; the rest of the evidence is on the [PDRN evidence hub](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/pdrn-research).
0.1% of PDRN-850K, a medium-length salmon PDRN (about 1,200 base pairs, up to 850 kDa), as the only active in an eye cream applied twice a day. The comparison side had 0.1% retinol in the same base.

It was published in the peer-reviewed journal PLOS ONE with no specific funding. Four of its authors are affiliated with commercial skincare biotechnology companies, and the paper declares no conflicts of interest.

Our [PDRN 1% Renewal Serum](https://www.skingenetix.com/products/pdrn-renewal-serum) contains 1% salmon PDRN; the trial used 0.1% of one specific medium-length PDRN in an eye cream. No study has compared PDRN concentrations, so a higher percentage should not be read as a bigger effect, and the trial's results are not our serum's results.

heading.en: What it means for our products

body.en: This trial is why PDRN is in our range as a skincare ingredient rather than only a clinic treatment: applied to intact skin, it improved crow's feet more than retinol did within four weeks, with no reactions in women with sensitive skin.

Our [PDRN 1% Renewal Serum](https://www.skingenetix.com/products/pdrn-renewal-serum) and [PDRN Collagen Night Cream](https://www.skingenetix.com/products/pdrn-collagen-night-cream) contain salmon PDRN. They are different formulas from the trial's eye cream, so we cite the trial for the ingredient as studied, not as a result our products have repeated. The rest of the evidence is on the [PDRN research hub](https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/pdrn-research).
